head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: The calendar update runs with the caller's credentials after the guests are saved, and it has no error handling.
reason: EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents (lines 845-869) loads the reference's credential from the database by credentialId when the caller doesn't hold it, and the work runs inside a try block, so non-organizer callers still update the organizer's calendar.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: The blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, so they can be bypassed.
reason: Line 71 lowercases only the blacklist entries, while lines 76-77 compare the raw `guest`, so a differently capitalised address gets past both the blacklist and the duplicate check.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: The emails are sent with the raw `guests` list instead of `uniqueGuests`.
reason: Line 168 passes the raw `guests`, and sendAddGuestsEmails uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (email-manager.ts:541), so existing attendees in the request are treated as new guests.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: The server never checks that guest emails are unique and does not limit how many can be sent.
reason: The schema is just `z.array(z.string().email())`, and `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing attendees, so repeated addresses in one request create duplicate rows and the list size is unbounded.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: The admin-or-owner check uses `&&`, so it only lets owners through.
reason: isTeamAdmin already matches ADMIN or OWNER (teams/index.ts:270), so `&& isTeamOwner` lets only owners through and plain admins are refused.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: The fallback error message can never be shown, and the invalid-email warning is never cleared.
reason: The template string at line 43 is never empty, so the fallback can't show, and isInvalidEmail is only reset by Cancel, so the warning stays after a fixed retry succeeds.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: A booking with no `userId` makes this call throw a generic 500 error.
reason: When booking.userId is null, an admin or attendee reaches `findFirstOrThrow` with `id: booking.userId || 0`, which throws a Prisma not-found error that reaches the client as an unhandled 500.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Dereferencing `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` crashes when there is no destination calendar.
reason: Line 118 sets `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it is undefined when there is no destination calendar, and line 119 then reads `.integration` without `?.`, which throws a TypeError for every Google Meet booking.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Unrelated change inverts when the organization slug is set.
reason: Line 151 is now `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which reverses the old `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }`, and this change has nothing to do with the destination calendar fix.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: The fallback lookup in `deleteEvent` never matches, so deletes go to "primary".
reason: Lines 315-317 only run the `find` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy and then compare against that same falsy value, so the lookup never matches and the delete falls back to "primary" instead of the destination calendar's externalId.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Video booking references no longer store `credentialId`.
reason: Line 170 `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the video credentialId, which the old code stored as `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: `updateAllCalendarEvents` now swallows the error without logging it.
reason: In the catch block at head (lines 591-608), `message` is built but never logged or returned, so calendar update failures leave no trace in the logs.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Team members' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has none.
reason: `destinationCalendar` falls back to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing and the other hosts' calendars are lost.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: `createEvent` ignores destination calendars that have no `credentialId` and writes to the primary calendar.
reason: CalendarManager passes `credential.id`, and Google `createEvent` picks a calendar only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, so a destination without a credentialId now goes to "primary" instead of its externalId.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Office365 always targets the main host's calendar id, including for other hosts' credentials.
reason: Office365 `createEvent` always posts to `/me/calendars/${destinationCalendar[0].externalId}/events`, even when `createAllCalendarEvents` calls it with another host's credential.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Events created for destinations without a credentialId lose their `externalCalendarId` in the references.
reason: Line 380 calls `createEvent(c, event)` without an externalId, and CalendarManager returns `externalId` straight from that parameter, so these references are saved with an undefined externalCalendarId.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: The `loadUsers` rewrite removes `organization.slug` from the dynamic-group user select.
reason: Nothing in handleNewBooking reads `organization.slug`; `getBookerUrl(organizerUser)` takes `organizationId` (getBookerUrl.ts line 4), so removing the select changes nothing.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: The CalDAV filter uses the main host's calendar, so no event is created for other hosts.
reason: Line 156 filters the CalDAV calendars by `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, the main host's calendar, so for another host's credential no calendar matches and no event is created.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: The users fallback lost its `|| []` default.
reason: `eventType.users` comes from a Prisma relation include, which always returns an array, so it cannot be undefined at line 755.

head: da09bc0808e7c6df1bc10e00d5acf764d94c7cc7
title: Caching tests deleted without replacement.
reason: The caching logic at lines 83-95 is unchanged and still checks `=== undefined` before rebuilding; deleting the tests loses coverage but breaks nothing, and the 'clean up tests' commit suggests the author meant to remove them.

head: da09bc0808e7c6df1bc10e00d5acf764d94c7cc7
title: Loose public options type removes compile-time checks on scope/teamId.
reason: A repo search finds `new InsightsBookingService` only in the integration test, so no caller can pass `{scope:'team'}` without `teamId` today, and the safeParse at line 62 makes bad options return the safe `1=0` condition.

head: da09bc0808e7c6df1bc10e00d5acf764d94c7cc7
title: Public `findMany` removed; callers outside this diff may break.
reason: A repo search shows InsightsBookingService is used only in insightsBooking.ts and its own test, so removing findMany breaks no caller.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: One failed SendGrid cancel stops the whole batch, and the rows already cancelled are never deleted.
reason: Lines 53-77 wrap the whole loop in one try, so a throw from `client.request` skips the remaining reminders, and the lazy Prisma deletes never run because `Promise.all` at line 74 is never reached.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: Reschedule still cancels emails right away through the 100-pending-cancellation SendGrid API.
reason: handleNewBooking.ts:968 passes immediateDelete=true; at emailReminderManager.ts:213-222 that POSTs the SendGrid cancel immediately and returns without setting `cancelled`, the capped path the PR says fails, and errors are only logged.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: Reminder cancellation is no longer awaited before the response is returned.
reason: handleCancelBooking.ts:485-493 calls the async delete helpers inside forEach without awaiting them, where the old code awaited the deletes via prismaPromises, so the `cancelled` update can be lost after the response is sent.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: Unrelated rework of the SMS verification UI in a reminder-cancellation fix.
reason: The change is the author's own 'small UI fix' commit, and the sender ID field is still rendered in its own block at lines 463-492, so nothing is lost by removing isSenderIdNeeded from the phone-number wrapper.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: Reminder cancellations on request-reschedule are fire-and-forget; the awaited deletes were removed.
reason: bookings.tsx:488-494 now calls the async helpers in forEach without awaiting them, where `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` used to run, so the `cancelled` update is fire-and-forget.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: With several override ranges on one day, every slot outside the first range is rejected.
reason: dateOverrides.find (lines 106-127) returns true for the first same-day override not containing the slot, so a slot covered only by a second range on that date is rejected.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: A slot inside a date override is marked available without checking busy times.
reason: Line 133 `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns before the busy.every check at line 153, so bookings/calendar events on override days are ignored.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: The working-hours check rejects a slot that falls outside any one entry, so split or midnight-crossing hours block everything.
reason: workingHours.find at lines 138-147 rejects if the slot is outside any single entry including the weekday, so per-user split hours (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17) reject every slot.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: `===` on two dayjs objects is never true, so zero-length (unavailable) overrides are not caught.
reason: Line 114 compares two distinct dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, so the zero-length override branch is dead and a slot starting exactly at that instant falls through as within the override.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: The override end check uses the slot's start, so slots that run past the override end are accepted.
reason: Line 123 checks slotStartTime.isAfter(end), so a slot starting inside the override but ending after it (or starting exactly at end) is accepted.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: `end` is computed from the slot start instead of the slot end.
reason: Line 142 computes `end` from slotStartTime, identical to `start`, so slots running past working-hour end are never rejected.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: Shifted override times can wrap past midnight, giving endTime < startTime.
reason: Lines 218-223 compute minutes-of-day after shifting, which wraps at midnight, while activeOverrides at 206-208 is filtered on the unshifted start, so overrides crossing the invitee's midnight yield endTime<startTime or wrong-day slots.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: Override dates are compared as UTC (or server-local) calendar days, not the organizer's local day.
reason: Lines 110-111 compare the override's shifted-to-UTC date string with the slot's UTC date, so for non-UTC organizers the override is matched to the wrong UTC day and slots inside it are missed or wrongly rejected.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: `override.timeZone` is optional, and when it is missing the server's default timezone is used.
reason: The only caller passing dateOverrides into getSlots is getSchedule (slots.ts:410-416), which always sets timeZone; TeamAvailabilityTimes callers pass only workingHours.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Migration crashes when the embed_category setting has no matching row.
reason: Line 9-11 indexes [0]['id'] on a query that returns no rows when embed_category is at its default or names a missing category; PG::Result#[] raises IndexError before the fallback runs.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Migrated hosts are not normalized, so existing embeds stop working.
reason: Line 25 inserts raw lines that skip the model's before_validation stripping, and record_for_host compares lower(host) to the bare uri.host; the new spec still uses 'http://discourse.org' and 'https://example.com/1234' as host values, which suggests the old setting accepted them.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: `before_validation` crashes when the host is nil.
reason: save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] directly, and when it is nil, self.host.sub! in before_validation raises NoMethodError, so the request returns a 500.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Host values are put into SQL without quoting.
reason: Line 25 puts '#{h}' into the SQL unescaped, so a stored value containing a quote breaks the migration.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: The settings are deleted inside a `change` migration, so a rollback loses the host list.
reason: This is a one-way data migration, and the raw execute calls in `change` are not reversible anyway, so a rollback raises an error instead of silently losing data.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Every `*_ids` key is now replaced, even when the referenced records were not side-loaded.
reason: The new _ids path only runs for __rest_serializer responses; the other users (queued posts, similar topics) send no *_ids keys, and the new EmbeddingSerializer has_many always sends the hosts along as an array.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: An unknown id causes a NoMethodError and a 500 response.
reason: update and destroy call methods on EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first, which is nil for an unknown id, so the request fails with NoMethodError and a 500.

head: 5b229316ee4c661836ed1161139692a3e8527444
title: Making `.small-action` a flex container stops `float: right` on its button from working.
reason: In small-action.hbs the buttons are inside .small-action-desc (lines 5 and 8), not direct flex children of .small-action, so their float: right still applies; .topic-avatar is first in the markup anyway.

head: 5b229316ee4c661836ed1161139692a3e8527444
title: A long topic title in the flex header can overflow and push the panel out of view.
reason: desktop/topic-post.scss:519 gives .extra-info-wrapper overflow: hidden, so it can shrink below its content width, and the .topic-link ellipsis rules (lines 532-537) keep truncating the title.

head: 5f8a130277dbddc95d133cd2832be639baf89213
title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so changing the case of the address gets around the block.
reason: `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` unchanged (user.rb:87), and nothing on User runs a before_validation step that lowercases it, so `where(email: email)` at blocked_email.rb:12 misses a blocked address typed in different case.

head: 5f8a130277dbddc95d133cd2832be639baf89213
title: The match_count update reads, adds and writes back, so concurrent matches overwrite each other.
reason: The `match_count += 1; save` at blocked_email.rb:14-16 is a read-modify-write that loses counts under concurrency, and `UsersController#create` runs validation twice (`user.valid?` at line 168 when call_discourse_hub is on, then `user.save`), so the counter goes up more than once per signup.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: Light-theme color for meta-data h5 links changes from 30% to 70% lightness, and the pair is inverted.
reason: The diff swaps `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for a light branch of 70% and a dark branch of 30%, the reverse of the X% to (100-X)% pattern used everywhere else, so light themes get paler links.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: Light-theme color for group member name changes from 30% to 50% lightness.
reason: The diff changes the light value of `.group-member-info .name` from 30% to 50%, so this text gets paler on light themes when the PR only meant to add a dark variant.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: Mobile custom-message-length light color changes from 70% to 30%, and the dark color is inverted.
reason: The diff changes the light value from 70% to 30% and the dark value to 70%, which inverts the colour on both light and dark themes.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: Mobile topic-map h3 light color changes from 20% to 50% lightness.
reason: The diff changes the light value of the mobile topic-map h3 from 20% to 50%, while the desktop sibling and the nearby `.number` rule keep (20%, 80%).

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: Mobile group member name light color changes from 30% to 50% lightness.
reason: The diff changes the light value of the mobile group-member name from 30% to 50%, which makes light themes paler.

head: ecfa17b5a79dfdc91e7a4d50b42ae78a35d0a293
title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the controller `set_locale`, not wherever translations are looked up.
reason: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called only in `set_locale` (application_controller.rb:159), and `translate` (translate_accelerator.rb:68) loads only `config.locale`, so Sidekiq jobs (jobs/base.rb:151) never load the `:en` fallback and the missing-translation result gets cached.

head: ecfa17b5a79dfdc91e7a4d50b42ae78a35d0a293
title: The fallback chain depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, but the translate cache key doesn't include it.
reason: The cache key at translate_accelerator.rb:72 leaves out the site default locale, and `@cache` is cleared only by `reload!`, which nothing calls when `default_locale` changes, so old fallback strings stay cached.

head: 303cdc2caf256aa5df660611120c2e3f7392365d
title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new logger, so logs written through it are never recorded
reason: No test pairs `TestLogger` with `LoggerMiddleware`: `NewTestLogger()` is only used in installer, bootstrap, process, pipeline and store tests, so nothing loses recorded logs. Returning a fresh instance also follows the fake's existing convention, since `New()` on line 19 does the same.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: The deprecated `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` no longer treats federated rule groups as read-only.
reason: The deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to check isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group); it now hands off to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which sets isFederated = false (line 245), so legacy callers such as RuleActionsButtons in RuleViewer and RulesTable will treat Mimir federated rules as editable.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: The `key` prop was dropped from the Grafana rule items in the filtered list.
reason: At head, FilterView.tsx lines 157-162 render <GrafanaRuleListItem> inside rules.map with no key prop, while the datasource and default branches still pass key={key}.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: The prom-based abilities now block Pause, Restore and Export for Grafana recording rules.
reason: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities ties ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently to prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule, while the ruler version used rulerRuleType.grafana.rule, which also covers recording rules, so Grafana recording rules in the list now lose Export.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: The list view loses the Delete and Pause actions for Grafana rules.
reason: GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule, and AlertRuleMenu shows Pause only when rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) is true (line 123) and Delete only when `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165), so both disappear from the list view.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: The provisioned check relies on a `provenance` field the Prometheus API may not return.
reason: The backend sends the field: pkg/services/ngalert/api/prometheus/api_prometheus.go:708 sets `Provenance: apimodels.Provenance(provenance)`, and prom.go:188 serialises it as json "provenance".

head: b1613e320acff00623e6efc59f00ee68c7684a97
title: Cache is not checked again after taking the write lock.
reason: After `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` (lines 48-49) the cache is not checked again, so every request that saw `ret == nil` reloads the manifest at line 60 one after another; this is a real redundant-work defect, even if small.

head: 04cfa3bfd469c035ff8b35f9a66867c4e8d5dcf4
title: Leftover debug logging at Error level dumps every batch's full ID list.
reason: Lines 534/537, 554/557 and 576/579 call r.log.Error on every batch, three of them with the full ids slice and an always-nil err; these are debugging leftovers that flood the error logs.

head: 04cfa3bfd469c035ff8b35f9a66867c4e8d5dcf4
title: Building the SQLite ID list with repeated Sprintf takes quadratic time.
reason: Line 611 `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` copies the growing string on every iteration, so building the list is quadratic in the batch size on the SQLite branch for batches over 999.

head: 04cfa3bfd469c035ff8b35f9a66867c4e8d5dcf4
title: The shared cleanup ticker now runs 10x as often, which the deadlock fix does not need.
reason: Line 77 changes the shared ticker to 1 minute, so every cleanup job runs ten times as often; the deadlock fix doesn't need this, only the auto-generated summary mentions it, and the 9-minute timeout in clean() still assumes a 10-minute cycle.

head: 04cfa3bfd469c035ff8b35f9a66867c4e8d5dcf4
title: Non-SQLite deletes bind one placeholder per ID, so very large batch sizes now fail.
reason: Lines 615-617 bind one `?` per ID on MySQL and Postgres, and cleanupjob_batchsize (setting.go:710) has no upper bound, so batch sizes over the 65535-placeholder limit now fail where the old subquery bound no parameters.

head: 26fed312840cd76b766cbd2158e17a7e6c0ec548
title: The storage-server integration test is now skipped on Postgres instead of fixed.
reason: The author skipped the test on purpose: the TODO at lines 35-37 and commit 6f4d7087 ('skips postgres integration test. Only fails in drone. Will fix later.') already explain it.

head: 26fed312840cd76b766cbd2158e17a7e6c0ec548
title: Removing `Init` from every handler means `Stop` no longer blocks requests.
reason: Stop (server.go:321-339) only sets s.initErr, which used to reach callers only through the per-handler s.Init calls this PR removed, so requests after Stop and IsHealthy are no longer rejected.

head: 26fed312840cd76b766cbd2158e17a7e6c0ec548
title: The new `TotalDocs` call reads the index cache map while the watcher may be writing to it.
reason: bleve.go TotalDocs (144-153) loops over b.cache without cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes b.cache[key] under the lock (137-139) and can run from the watcher goroutine started at search.go:207, before the new TotalDocs call at line 216.

head: e944e2acf1e64421860a8e827f93ad06c169621b
title: Test cleanup removes a provider named "alias" instead of the ones it created.
reason: Lines 381 and 425 register `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`, which targets the literal alias "alias", so the `idp-alias-N` providers the test creates are never cleaned up.

head: e944e2acf1e64421860a8e827f93ad06c169621b
title: Login IDP cache is not cleared when an organization is enabled or disabled.
reason: The default `getForLogin` (IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:165-184) filters only on IDP enabled, link-only, hide-on-login, broker-public and organization ID; it never checks whether the organization is enabled, and the JPA provider has no override, so the premise is false.

head: 7355f05e6aafe2a7acc6434fb40c686665416606
title: canManage() lets an admin with only the `view` scope manage groups.
reason: GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() Javadoc (lines 73-78) explicitly documents 'For V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups', so accepting VIEW is the documented, intended behaviour.

head: 7355f05e6aafe2a7acc6434fb40c686665416606
title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource IDs where group IDs are expected.
reason: ResourceStore.create(server, name, owner) passes id=null and JPAResourceStore.create generates a new ID (line 66), so groupResource.getId() is not the group ID; findByName(groupResource.getId()) misses and falls back to the all-groups resource, and resource IDs are returned instead of group IDs.

head: 1950a511026d520a7329c7b6b9ee60a4af8f8b55
title: canExchangeTo and other reachable methods now throw UnsupportedOperationException under V2.
reason: AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the v2 feature is on, and its clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException (lines 147-150); legacy token exchange calls it at AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276, so the request fails with a 500 instead of a 403.

head: 1950a511026d520a7329c7b6b9ee60a4af8f8b55
title: Missing "Clients" type resource causes an NPE instead of a denial.
reason: getResourceTypeResource only looks the resource up with findByName and returns null when it is missing (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:116-133); init() returns early for realms that already have an admin-permissions client, and the cached findByResource then calls resource.getId() on null (StoreFactoryCacheSession.java:938), giving a 500 instead of a denial.

head: 4def149a50c4b9b2c24fbb753ac60fe4f4df0cac
title: The reader thread keeps running forever if a delete throws.
reason: deletedAll.set(true) at line 155 is only reached if every remove() at line 153 succeeds; if one throws, the reader thread started at line 139 is never stopped and keeps calling groups(...) in a loop.

head: 4def149a50c4b9b2c24fbb753ac60fe4f4df0cac
title: The test checks for errors without waiting for the reader thread to finish.
reason: No reference to the thread is kept and it is never joined, so the assertion at line 157 can pass before the reader's last request records its exception.

head: 4def149a50c4b9b2c24fbb753ac60fe4f4df0cac
title: Groups created so far are left in the shared realm if creation fails partway.
reason: The helper createGroup in AbstractGroupTest (lines 54-57) registers each group with managedRealm.cleanup(), but this test calls groups().add directly and registers nothing, so groups stay behind in the shared realm if creation or deletion fails partway.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: `isAccessTokenId` never checks the grant shortcut: it reads the wrong offset and the condition is inverted.
reason: The decoder reads the grant shortcut with encodedContext.substring(4, 6), but the matcher at AssertEvents.java:483 uses substring(3, 5) and returns false on a match, so the grant is never actually checked.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: New abstract `getShortcut()` breaks custom grant providers; the Javadoc's "3-letter" guidance produces IDs that can't be decoded, and a null shortcut breaks startup.
reason: All in-repo OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations are in services/ under the private SPI, so none breaks; the '3-letters' Javadoc wording is a doc remark.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: The null check meant for `rawTokenId` checks `grantType` again.
reason: Line 73 calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), so it checks grantType twice and a null rawTokenId is never rejected.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: Public copy constructor `Context(Context)` removed with no reason given in the request.
reason: Nothing in the repo uses the removed Context(Context) copy constructor (grant types call setContext(context)), the class is private SPI, and no caller is shown passing null formParams.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: OptimizedCursorPaginator calls math.floor/ceil on a datetime key and uses raw cursor values.
reason: get_item_key (line 840) calls math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, 'datetime') since the endpoint orders by -datetime, raising TypeError, and value_from_cursor returns the raw int unlike DateTimePaginator (lines 233-241).

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: The negative-offset branch slices a Django queryset with a negative index, and its comment describes reaching data beyond pagination bounds.
reason: Line 882 slices the queryset with a client-supplied negative cursor.offset; Django querysets reject negative indexing, so this is a client-triggerable 500 when the flag is enabled.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: Switching the buffer keys from sets to sorted sets has no migration path for keys already in Redis.
reason: add-buffer.lua and buffer.py now use zcard/zunionstore/zadd/zscan on the same span-buf:s key names previously written as SETs, so existing keys or old consumers during rollout produce WRONGTYPE errors.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: The admin gate fails with an AttributeError when member is None, and has_global_access does not mean admin.
reason: RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (model.py:346), and line 71 dereferences it unconditionally for non-superusers on every request; has_global_access is a default-true member flag, not an admin scope.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: BasePaginator offset handling is changed for every paginator, but negative offsets are still passed through for prev cursors.
reason: Before the change the prev-cursor path already sliced with the raw offset; the new line 182 only adds clamping for non-prev cursors, so nothing is made worse.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: The redirect depth limit drops from 10000 to 1000 with no reason given.
reason: The depth cap reduction is part of the upstream eviction commit, and with segments now capped at 1000 spans it is an intentional tuning change, not a defect.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: Spans past 1000 are silently evicted, possibly including the segment root, with no metric or log.
reason: The commit message states eviction by oldest end timestamp is the intended design; the hardcoded 1000 still matches the configured max_segment_spans default of 1001, and the missing metric is an observability remark.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: A missing end_timestamp_precise raises KeyError and stops the consumer.
reason: end_timestamp_precise is treated as a required SpanEvent field throughout the span consumers (enrichment.py:89,117,162; message.py:121,191,227) by direct indexing, so the field is always present.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: With the feature flag on, table widgets always render empty.
reason: The empty TableWidgetVisualization only renders behind the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag, and commit 4c997de2 says this is part 1, with replacing widget tables coming in part 2.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Hidden attributes are filtered out only while a search query is set.
reason: Lines 61-63 return `sorted` before the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter, so the hidden attributes still show when the search box is empty.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Saved-search migrations turned into no-ops, pointing to a 0921 migration this PR does not add.
reason: 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised exists: 0922 depends on it and it has its own test file.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Comment says the revised migration was never run, but this one already had the null-owner fix.
reason: Migration 0921 exists (0922 depends on it and tests/sentry/migrations/test_0921_... covers it), so the conversion is not lost.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Zipping error_ids with get_multi values can pair IDs with the wrong events.
reason: nodestore get_multi builds the dict from service results and then runs `items.update(cache_items)`, so when only some ids are cached the values order differs from error_ids and the zip pairs ids with the wrong events.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Error timestamps in seconds are compared with replay event timestamps in milliseconds.
reason: Error timestamps from event data are epoch seconds while rrweb replay events use milliseconds, so the `<` comparison at lines 153-155 emits every error before the first event.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: The detector owner is not checked against the detector's organization.
reason: ActorField.to_internal_value calls parse_and_validate_actor(data, self.context['organization'].id), which validates the owner against the organization.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: The attribute-keys query no longer turns off retries or window-focus refetching.
reason: DEFAULT_QUERY_CLIENT_CONFIG already sets refetchOnWindowFocus: false, so the claimed refetch on focus does not happen; the remaining retry difference is minor.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Second placeholder group loses its gap and vertical alignment.
reason: The removed FlexBox applied align-items:center and gap:space(1) to both groups, but the new second `<Flex>` (line 27) and the loaded container (line 93) leave them out, which changes the layout.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Writable aggregate fields that are still `Visualize` instances are now dropped from the ref counts and serialized wrongly.
reason: Every setVisualizes caller (toolbarVisualize, charts/index, aggregateColumnEditorModal) converts with `.toJSON()`, and the setter is typed BaseVisualize[].

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Unrelated change to the auth task's processing deadline.
reason: Commit b4d30008 'Extend deadlines for check_auth' explains this change; it is a scope remark, not a defect.

head: 9501091c52ae94e8d916f79b35d21975b3f9cadb
title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time, so every instance gets the same timestamp.
reason: Line 18 `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs once when the class is defined, so every instance built without an explicit `queued` (including every one from `from_integration`) carries the same import-time timestamp.

head: 9501091c52ae94e8d916f79b35d21975b3f9cadb
title: Task kwargs now include a raw `datetime`, which a JSON task serializer cannot encode.
reason: src/sentry/conf/server.py:739 sets CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "pickle", which encodes the datetime without error and returns it as a datetime, so neither the enqueue failure nor the string round-trip happens.

head: dcdcadb771128e79259cc9eff9c70c38fc597976
title: Names removed from mark_failed may still be imported or patched elsewhere.
reason: A repository search shows the only remaining imports from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed (in check_missed, check_timeout, monitor_consumer and two test files) import just `mark_failed`, which still exists, and no reference or mock.patch to mark_failed_threshold or any other removed name remains.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: Closing the strategy shuts down the factory's shared queue pool, so messages after a rebalance are dropped and committed.
reason: result_consumer.py:133 creates one FixedQueuePool in the factory and every strategy reuses it, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() calls queue_pool.shutdown(); after that, put() raises queue.ShutDown, and the except in submit marks the offset complete, so the message is committed without being processed.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: The queues have no size limit, so there is no backpressure and memory can grow without bound.
reason: Line 185 creates `queue.Queue()` with no maxsize and submit never raises MessageRejected, so nothing pushes back on Kafka and the docstring's "Natural backpressure when queues fill up" is not true.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: A gap in Kafka offsets stops all further commits for that partition.
reason: Stopping commits at a gap is deliberate: test_offset_gaps_block_commits in test_queue_consumer.py:351 and test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps check for it, and the finding only assumes the uptime results topic has gaps without showing it.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: Offsets are committed from a background thread, including for partitions that may have been revoked.
reason: _commit_loop calls arroyo's commit callable from its own daemon thread, outside the poll/submit cycle on the processor thread, and the factory-level offset_tracker is never cleared on rebalance, so it can commit offsets for partitions this consumer no longer owns.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: `close()` stops committing before the workers finish, so finished work is never committed and gets reprocessed.
reason: close() sets shutdown_event and joins the commit thread before queue_pool.shutdown(), and each worker stops at `while not self.shutdown` without draining its queue, so finished work is never committed and queued items are dropped.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: The error-handling test asserts no commit happens, which contradicts the implementation and only passes by timing.
reason: Both offsets get completed in the worker's finally, so the 1s commit tick can commit offset 102 during the 0.2s+ wait; the assertion at line 1922 therefore depends on timing and checks the opposite of what the docstring says.
